scope: Fresh30natural+30synthetic wheel fact-mask replication. Exact0040 wheel-only question. Original native missing-pedal rejections retained; strict raw wheel scoring only, no native/live qualification or actuation.
wheel_task: WHEEL TASK: Select the single allowed absolute wheel ID whose supplied policy condition holds. Return only that wheel choice.
common_definitions: Apply the following fixed bearing policy to the CURRENT factual state; its eligible wheel and pedal form one native input. These are supplied engineering rules, not a claim that the input is optimal or pursuit-equivalent. Read x=ego_x_m and y=ego_y_m from the road.preview row whose ahead_m equals 15, using road.preview_columns. The 15 m centre bearing theta equals round(degrees(atan2(y,x)),4), calculated from those rounded raw coordinates. If road.preview_15m_bearing_deg is present, read theta directly from that factual scalar; otherwise compute theta yourself. Positive theta means LEFT of the kart nose, negative theta means RIGHT. Thresholds are -22, -7, +7 and +22 degrees; exact threshold ties choose the smaller absolute wheel angle. Let speed=kart.speed_m_s and L=current_road_frame.velocity_left_m_s. Let B be true exactly when road.on_road is false, OR (road.offset_m>0 AND road.left_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L>=0.5), OR (road.offset_m<0 AND road.right_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L<=-0.5). Otherwise B is false. The speed<2 acceleration rule takes priority even when B is true.

Apply the following fixed bearing policy to the CURRENT factual state; its eligible wheel and pedal form one native input. Read x=ego_x_m and y=ego_y_m from the road.preview row whose ahead_m equals 15, using road.preview_columns. If road.preview_15m_bearing_deg is present, read theta directly from that factual scalar; otherwise compute theta yourself. Positive theta means LEFT of the kart nose, negative theta means RIGHT. wheel.instructions:
DRIVING POLICY. Choose the next native input by executing the supplied policy exactly. Apply the following fixed bearing policy to the CURRENT factual state; its eligible wheel and pedal form one native input. These are supplied engineering rules, not a claim that the input is optimal or pursuit-equivalent. Read x=ego_x_m and y=ego_y_m from the road.preview row whose ahead_m equals 15, using road.preview_columns. The 15 m centre bearing theta equals round(degrees(atan2(y,x)),4), calculated from those rounded raw coordinates. If road.preview_15m_bearing_deg is present, read theta directly from that factual scalar; otherwise compute theta yourself. Positive theta means LEFT of the kart nose, negative theta means RIGHT. Thresholds are -22, -7, +7 and +22 degrees; exact threshold ties choose the smaller absolute wheel angle. Let speed=kart.speed_m_s and L=current_road_frame.velocity_left_m_s. Let B be true exactly when road.on_road is false, OR (road.offset_m>0 AND road.left_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L>=0.5), OR (road.offset_m<0 AND road.right_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L<=-0.5). Otherwise B is false. The speed<2 acceleration rule takes priority even when B is true.
WHEEL TASK: Select the single allowed absolute wheel ID whose supplied policy condition holds. Return only that wheel choice.

If road.preview_15m_bearing_deg is present, read theta directly from that factual scalar; otherwise compute theta yourself. Positive theta means LEFT of the kart nose, negative theta means RIGHT. wheel.instructions:
DRIVING POLICY. Choose the next native input by executing the supplied policy exactly. Apply the following fixed bearing policy to the CURRENT factual state; its eligible wheel and pedal form one native input. These are supplied engineering rules, not a claim that the input is optimal or pursuit-equivalent. Read x=ego_x_m and y=ego_y_m from the road.preview row whose ahead_m equals 15, using road.preview_columns. The 15 m centre bearing theta equals round(degrees(atan2(y,x)),4), calculated from those rounded raw coordinates. If road.preview_15m_bearing_deg is present, read theta directly from that factual scalar; otherwise compute theta yourself. Positive theta means LEFT of the kart nose, negative theta means RIGHT. Thresholds are -22, -7, +7 and +22 degrees; exact threshold ties choose the smaller absolute wheel angle. Let speed=kart.speed_m_s and L=current_road_frame.velocity_left_m_s. Let B be true exactly when road.on_road is false, OR (road.offset_m>0 AND road.left_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L>=0.5), OR (road.offset_m<0 AND road.right_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L<=-0.5). Otherwise B is false. The speed<2 acceleration rule takes priority even when B is true.
WHEEL TASK: Select the single allowed absolute wheel ID whose supplied policy condition holds. Return only that wheel choice.

wheel.instructions:
DRIVING POLICY. Choose the next native input by executing the supplied policy exactly. Apply the following fixed bearing policy to the CURRENT factual state; its eligible wheel and pedal form one native input. These are supplied engineering rules, not a claim that the input is optimal or pursuit-equivalent. Read x=ego_x_m and y=ego_y_m from the road.preview row whose ahead_m equals 15, using road.preview_columns. The 15 m centre bearing theta equals round(degrees(atan2(y,x)),4), calculated from those rounded raw coordinates. If road.preview_15m_bearing_deg is present, read theta directly from that factual scalar; otherwise compute theta yourself. Positive theta means LEFT of the kart nose, negative theta means RIGHT. Thresholds are -22, -7, +7 and +22 degrees; exact threshold ties choose the smaller absolute wheel angle. Let speed=kart.speed_m_s and L=current_road_frame.velocity_left_m_s. Let B be true exactly when road.on_road is false, OR (road.offset_m>0 AND road.left_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L>=0.5), OR (road.offset_m<0 AND road.right_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L<=-0.5). Otherwise B is false. The speed<2 acceleration rule takes priority even when B is true.
WHEEL TASK: Select the single allowed absolute wheel ID whose supplied policy condition holds. Return only that wheel choice.

current_road_frame.units: Angles are degrees and velocities are m/s in the CURRENT ROAD frame. Positive nose_vs_road_deg and velocity_vs_road_deg mean LEFT of the current road tangent. Positive velocity_left_m_s means LEFT; positive velocity_forward_m_s means FORWARD along that tangent.

wheel.instructions:
DRIVING POLICY. Choose the next native input by executing the supplied policy exactly. Apply the following fixed bearing policy to the CURRENT factual state; its eligible wheel and pedal form one native input. These are supplied engineering rules, not a claim that the input is optimal or pursuit-equivalent. Read x=ego_x_m and y=ego_y_m from the road.preview row whose ahead_m equals 15, using road.preview_columns. The 15 m centre bearing theta equals round(degrees(atan2(y,x)),4), calculated from those rounded raw coordinates. If road.preview_15m_bearing_deg is present, read theta directly from that factual scalar; otherwise compute theta yourself. Positive theta means LEFT of the kart nose, negative theta means RIGHT. Thresholds are -22, -7, +7 and +22 degrees; exact threshold ties choose the smaller absolute wheel angle. Let speed=kart.speed_m_s and L=current_road_frame.velocity_left_m_s. Let B be true exactly when road.on_road is false, OR (road.offset_m>0 AND road.left_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L>=0.5), OR (road.offset_m<0 AND road.right_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L<=-0.5). Otherwise B is false. The speed<2 acceleration rule takes priority even when B is true.
WHEEL TASK: Select the single allowed absolute wheel ID whose supplied policy condition holds. Return only that wheel choice.

criteria.hard_left: Hold wheels LEFT at 6.88 degrees; a nominal bicycle turn radius of 14.9 metres before grip/response transients. FIXED POLICY ELIGIBILITY: choose this wheel exactly when theta > +22 degrees.
criteria.left: Hold wheels LEFT at 3.44 degrees; a nominal bicycle turn radius of 30.0 metres before grip/response transients. FIXED POLICY ELIGIBILITY: choose this wheel exactly when +7 < theta <= +22 degrees.

criteria.right: Hold wheels RIGHT at 3.44 degrees; a nominal bicycle turn radius of 30.0 metres before grip/response transients. FIXED POLICY ELIGIBILITY: choose this wheel exactly when -22 <= theta < -7 degrees.
criteria.hard_right: Hold wheels RIGHT at 6.88 degrees; a nominal bicycle turn radius of 14.9 metres before grip/response transients. FIXED POLICY ELIGIBILITY: choose this wheel exactly when theta < -22 degrees.
